## ⚠️ SERIAL — a sibling is live in your directory

**#5725 is IN FLIGHT in the SAME subtree**, `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/` — its files are **`view-column-io.ts`** + its tests + the pin in `ViewColumnInspector.identityRead.test.tsx`. ## 裁决 — triage's direction

Triage seat, 2026-08-24 (finding concentration round), → `pm:queue` / Task (S). Verbatim: *"Give the canvas an icon/tone source that covers renderable-but-unoffered types (e.g. `record:chatter`): **consult the renderer registry (or extend `BLOCK_TYPE_META` with a non-palette entry class)** instead of falling to the unknown-block icon for types the page can legitimately contain."*

## The mechanism, and the one constraint that shapes every fix

`PageBlockCanvas.tsx` draws icon and tone from the **palette** catalogue:

```
const meta = BLOCK_TYPE_META[typeStr as BlockTypeId];
const Icon = meta?.Icon ?? UnknownBlockIcon;
const tone = resolveBlockTone(typeStr);   // -> BLOCK_CATEGORY_TONE['misc'] on a miss
```

⭐ **`BLOCK_TYPE_META` answers "what may an author drag in". The canvas is asking "what may an author already have in this page".** Two different questions, one list. That framing is the card's real contribution and it should drive the fix.

For exclusions whose reason is *"no renderer"* (`ai:chat_window`, `element:form`, `element:record_picker`, `element:text_input`) the generic box is arguably **right** — those nodes genuinely do not render. ⚠️ **One exclusion is different:** `record:chatter` / `record:discussion` is excluded *because the pair is one renderer under two names*, so **exactly one of the two spellings is always an unoffered type that renders perfectly**. It draws `UnknownBlockIcon` and the neutral `misc` grey where its twin one line above gets `MessageSquare` and the blue `record` tone.

⛔ **The hard constraint:** `block-config.test.ts`'s *"no type is both offered and excluded"* must keep holding. **That is why this cannot simply be a second `BLOCK_TYPE_META` entry** — the card says so explicitly, and it is the trap that makes the obvious fix wrong.

The card names two shapes; ✅ either is acceptable and you choose on measurement:
1. a small **alias→canonical display map** consulted when `BLOCK_TYPE_META` misses, so an unoffered-but-renderable type borrows its twin's icon and tone **without becoming offerable**;
2. **split the catalogue** into *display meta* (every type the canvas can encounter) and *palette offer list* (the subset an author may drag) — two questions, two lists.

⚠️ (2) is the honest shape and (1) is the small one. If (2) turns out to be more than an S card's worth, take (1) and **say so**, naming (2) as the follow-up.

## PM mechanism assumptions — measure, do not assume

1. **The card is from 2026-08-23 and `packages/app-shell` moved twice today** (#6031, #6035). Re-derive the `BLOCK_TYPE_META` read, `resolveBlockTone`, and the `PALETTE_EXCLUSIONS` ledger on your merge-base; report any delta.
2. ⚠️ **Which spelling is currently unoffered is a moving fact.** Before #5495 it was the **canonical** `record:discussion` — the one `plugin-detail/src/synth/buildDefaultPageSchema.ts` emits, i.e. in every page the platform generates for itself. After #5495 it is the legacy `record:chatter`. ⛔ Do not hard-code either; the fix must work whichever way the pair is oriented, or a future flip re-opens this.
3. **`blockLabel()` is NOT affected** — it never reads `BLOCK_TYPE_META` and falls back to the raw type string. ⛔ The gap is **icon + tone only**; do not widen into labels.
4. ⚠️ **Do not make the "no renderer" exclusions borrow an icon.** They are correctly generic. A fix keyed on "is excluded" rather than "is renderable" would give `element:text_input` a friendly icon it has not earned. Key on **renderability**, and say how you determined it.

## Verification

Direction predicted **before** running: a page carrying the **unoffered** spelling of the pair must draw the same icon and tone as its offered twin; revert and show the pin goes red.

**Counter-probes, three, and they are the fix's whole safety margin:** (a) `block-config.test.ts`'s *"no type is both offered and excluded"* must **stay green** — run it explicitly and quote it; (b) a genuinely unrenderable exclusion (`element:text_input`) must **still** draw `UnknownBlockIcon` and `misc`; (c) the palette's offer list must be **unchanged** — nothing became draggable. ⛔ Without (c), "the icon appears" is satisfiable by quietly making the type offerable, which is the exact invariant #2943 made an explicit ledger to protect.

Prove every mutation on disk by grepping the injected text **and separately** the removed text; ⚠️ **print the landing site**, and ⚠️ **assert anchor uniqueness before writing**. Restore under `trap … EXIT INT TERM` with a **cwd-independent** restore command — a trap that fires is not a trap that restored (measured on #5926 today). Confirm `git diff HEAD --stat` empty afterwards.

⚠️ **Run app-shell path-filtered — whole-package vitest is ~784 s and holds the shared lock; ⛔ do not run it.** Gates by name with exit codes: `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (⚠️ hyphenated; echo the script name; distinguish the **unbuilt-closure** red from the **missing-`node_modules`** red — both hit today, different fixes), the path-filtered vitest **including `block-config.test.ts`**, eslint on changed files with merge-base delta. ⚠️ Plain `eslint .` per package — ⛔ no `--no-inline-config`.

Run `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` rather than guessing. Draft PR, `Fixes #5837`. ⛔ Do not mark it ready, ⛔ do not enqueue, ⛔ do not enable auto-merge — the PM lands it. Post the terminal report here (plain-text first-line marker `os-dev-report`; ⛔ avoid short angle-bracket placeholders in prose — the sanitizer ate one on #5926 today) and return it.

## Notes for the PM, outside the JSON

**PM assumption checks.**
1. Re-derived on merge-base `a1c41c516` after #6031/#6035: the `BLOCK_TYPE_META` read, `resolveBlockTone` and the `PALETTE_EXCLUSIONS` ledger are **exactly** as the card quotes them. No delta.

So for the discussion/chatter pair specifically, the user-visible symptom today is the **badge tone**, not the icon. Both halves are fixed and pinned — the DOM icon probe uses container-shaped nodes to reach that branch — but the card's "icon + tone" reads as one symptom when today it is one-and-a-latent-one.

## PM review — **ACCEPT**

PR #6072, head `7114898f0`, merge-base `a1c41c516`. Gate read at the usual mark.

### ⭐ Assumption 4 was the trap, and #6071 shows it was a live one

I wrote: *"⛔ Do not make the 'no renderer' exclusions borrow an icon. A fix keyed on **is excluded** rather than **is renderable** would give `element:text_input` a friendly icon it has not earned. Key on **renderability**, and say how you determined it."*

You keyed on something stricter than I asked for — **renderer identity**: a group may only list spellings that `ComponentRegistry.getConfig` resolves to the **very same component function**, asserted against the real registry, **identity rather than both-defined**. And then you found why that mattered:

> **#6071** — two `PALETTE_EXCLUSIONS` reason strings say *"no renderer"* for block types that **DO** have registered renderers: `element:text_input` (`text-input.tsx:161`) and `element:record_picker` (`record-picker.tsx:303`).
> *"This is exactly why the fix keys on renderer identity within an alias group rather than on bare registration — **a registry-membership key would have handed those two an icon and broken counter-probe (b)**."*

⛔ So the obvious reading of my own instruction — "renderable = registered" — would have **failed**, on two of the four exclusions I told you to protect. ✅ The finding is not a side observation; it is the evidence that the design choice was necessary. And the accompanying detail is sharp: **`block-config.test.ts` enforces that a reason EXISTS, never that it is true** — so a ledger built to be explicit (#2943) carries two false clauses that no gate can see. ✅ Correctly scoped, too: the *substantive* half of each reason (*"bare inputs belong to a form"*, *"record picking is a field widget"*) is still correct and still the decision; only the leading clause is false — and `core/src/registry/public-blocks.ts` already words the same two exclusions without it. ✅ And `element:form` explicitly **not** claimed either way, because it was not checked closely enough. Declining to assert about the one you did not measure is what makes the two you did assert trustworthy.

### The two other assumptions, enforced structurally rather than by care

✅ **Assumption 2 (which spelling is unoffered is a moving fact):** no orientation is hard-coded — every assertion derives the offered/unoffered split from `BLOCK_TYPE_META`, and **one test flips the catalogue outright** (try/finally, restoration asserted) to prove the resolver follows if #5495's ruling is ever reversed. ⛔ A comment saying "don't hard-code the orientation" would have rotted; a test that flips it cannot.

✅ **Assumption 3 (do not widen into labels):** `BlockDisplayMeta` deliberately carries **only `Icon` and `category`, no `label`** — so display resolution *structurally cannot* reach `blockLabel()`. That is the instruction made unbreakable rather than obeyed.

### The measured correction to the card's own symptom

> the canvas draws a node's icon only in its **container** branch (`isContainer`); a leaf node gets a live preview plus a type badge, **so for the discussion/chatter pair the visible symptom today is the badge TONE, not the icon**

✅ The card describes the icon as the visible defect. It is half right, and only measurement would show which half. Both are fixed and pinned, with the **DOM icon probe using container-shaped nodes to reach that branch** — otherwise the icon pin would have been asserting against a branch the fixture never enters, which is a vacuous pin wearing a DOM assertion's clothes.

### Shape choice and counter-probes

✅ **Shape (1) taken, shape (2) named as the follow-up in the PR body** — exactly the instruction for the case where the honest shape exceeds an S card. ⛔ Silently taking (1) without naming (2) is how a catalogue stays conflated for another year.

All three counter-probes run and quoted:
- **(a)** `'✓ … no type is both offered and excluded 0ms'` — quoted verbatim from the run, not summarised. That invariant (#2943's) was the hard constraint.
- **(b)** the four genuinely-unrenderable exclusions keep `undefined` meta and `BLOCK_CATEGORY_TONE.misc`, ✅ **and the DOM probe asserts `element:text_input`'s badge keeps the zinc misc classes in the SAME render where the pair is fixed** — one render, both outcomes, so the two cannot drift apart.
- **(c)** the drag-in list derived from `BLOCK_TYPE_META`, no `PALETTE_EXCLUSIONS` key draggable, plus a dedicated *"no alias-group member became offerable"*. ⛔ That was the probe I said the fix's whole safety margin rests on, and it is two probes rather than one.

✅ The ablation matched the prediction **exactly** — 4 failed / 37 passed, the four fix pins red by name while (a) and (c) stayed green. ✅ Anchor uniqueness asserted before writing with the **landing byte offset (14733) and line (310) printed**; injected and removed text grepped separately; trap armed **before** the mutation, cwd-independent, printing `TRAP: restore rc=0`, with `git diff HEAD --stat` empty and both greps inverted afterwards. ✅ And "no rebuild leg was needed and none is claimed" with the reason — the suite imports `../block-types` relatively, *"this is not an exports-resolved pair"*.

✅ The first type-check failure was correctly identified as **a syntax error you had introduced** (TS1002/TS1005 in the new test file) and distinguished from *both* the unbuilt-closure red and the missing-`node_modules` red. Three red signatures, told apart by reading them.

## PM review — **ACCEPT**, enqueued

PR **#6072** read at head, gates read **once** at 15:52Z off the run's own `started_at` (15:35:06Z, ~17 min elapsed — deliberately late rather than early; three reads in this round were taken too early and had to be re-armed).

**Gate reading: 22 checks, 19 success + 3 skipped, 0 failing, 0 still running.** ⚠️ Read as **every check green, not the required subset** — `Test (shard 1..4/4)`, `Type Check`, `Lint`, `Build & E2E`, `Build Docs`, `Bundle Analysis`, `Doc Snippet Type Check`, `Doc Component Type Check`, `Internal Docs Link Check`, `Skill Guide Path Check`, `Control Byte Scan`, `Changeset Declaration` / `Fixed Group` / `Bump Policy`, `Live E2E (informational)`, `label`. The three `skipped` are the coverage jobs and `dependabot`, which are conditional on this event type.

**Not a governed surface.** Four files, all under `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/` plus the changeset. No `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. Marked ready and enqueued through the merge queue; ⛔ nothing was merged by hand.

### What earned the accept

The fix is keyed on **renderer identity**, not on "is excluded" — and the suite makes that claim falsifiable rather than asserting it in prose:

- `BLOCK_RENDERER_ALIAS_GROUPS` may only list spellings that resolve through the **real `ComponentRegistry`** to the *same component object* (`toBe`, not "both defined"). Two independently registered renderers that happened to look alike would pass a defined/defined check and fail this one.
- The lookup itself carries a **non-vacuity control** — `config('record:zzNotARegisteredType')` must be `undefined`, so a `getConfig` that returned something truthy for anything cannot make the identity assertions meaningless.
- **The counter-probe is the part that matters most.** `element:text_input`, `element:record_picker`, `element:form`, `ai:chat_window` are excluded for reasons that have nothing to do with aliasing, have no twin, and are asserted to keep the generic box and the `misc` tone. A fix keyed on "is excluded" would have handed all four an icon they have not earned — and would still have passed the positive half.
- **No orientation is hard-coded.** #5495 already flipped which member of the pair the palette advertises; every assertion derives the offered/unoffered split from `BLOCK_TYPE_META` rather than naming a side, and one test flips the catalogue outright to prove the resolver follows — restoring in `finally` and then *asserting the restore* (`offered[wasOffered]).toBe(saved)`), so a leaked mutation cannot silently re-colour every later assertion in the process.
- **The invariant #2943 exists to protect is pinned separately.** "The icon appears" is also satisfiable by quietly making the type draggable; the third describe block asserts `TYPES_BY_CATEGORY` is exactly `Object.keys(BLOCK_TYPE_META)` and that no exclusion became draggable. The offer list is unchanged, and that is measured, not claimed.
- The DOM leg asserts the tone class on the badge **and** the icon class on the row, each with the un-twinned exclusion rendered in the *same* render as an in-frame control — so "both fell through to grey" cannot pass as "both share the record tone".

The side-effect import of `@object-ui/plugin-detail` is called out in the test file as deliberate (the app-shell setup does not pull it in, and depending on another file having imported it first would make the suite order-dependent). That is the right call and the right reason.

### Noted, not blocking

- `BlockDisplayMeta` is deliberately **narrower** than `BlockTypeMeta` — no `label` — with the reason stated: `blockLabel()` never consulted the catalogue, and widening display resolution into labels would change author-visible naming, which is a separate decision. Correct fencing.
- Changeset is `patch` on `@object-ui/app-shell`. The new names are additive, not a break, so `patch` is right and `Changeset Bump Policy` agrees; ⛔ `major` is refused by this repo outright regardless.
- **#6071** (`PALETTE_EXCLUSIONS` reasons say "no renderer" for two block types that *do* have registered renderers) was filed rather than folded in. Right call — it is a different defect class (stale *reason prose* in the ledger) and folding it would have widened this PR past its fence.
